subject: how to predict the stochastic volatility

messages.author: 0855a3b8b153f658
messages.subject: how to predict the stochastic volatility
parts:
hi, all
 
In the manual of the INLA program, section 3 for the SV model, in order to predict the volatility,  n set to be 1001 which is greater than the number of returns in the "Predictor
 
term" in .ini file. But how to imply this in the R-INLA program?
 
Another question is even we can predict the volatility, we can not get the predictive distribution of return directly from the INLA, is it right?  do we need to write another program
 
for the predictive distribution ?
 
Best Regards
 
George

messages.author: 8be293492d512f32
messages.subject: Re: how to predict the stochastic volatility
parts:
hi
to get the predicted marginal for the linear predictor you have to add one line to your data set as it is explained in the FAQ 

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-How-can-I-do-predictions-using-INLA-

You then get the marginal posterior for the linear predictor. If you want to get the marginal for the return in order to compute the VaR then you have to solve the one dimensional integral that is in equation 4 of the volatility paper

http://www.math.ntnu.no/~hrue/r-inla.org/papers/stochvol-nr.pdf

for this you have to write your own code as it is not included in the INLA library

Hope this helps

sara
